form.title: Supporting Transitioning Foster Youth: Final Report Cover Sheet

form_text:
VICTORIA S. AND BRADLEY L. GEIST FOUNDATION
827 FORT STREET • HONOLULU • HAWAI`I • 96813 • (808) 537-6333
Supporting Transitioning Foster Youth Final Report (or Progress Report) Cover Sheet
The Trustees appreciate your work and look forward to learning more about it. Your final report provides important information that helps the Trustees to evaluate the Foundation’s programs. Your candor about what worked and why -- and what didn’t work and why not -- makes your report valuable and appreciated.
Your report is due no later than 13 months after the date of your grant award letter. The Foundation does not accept proposals from organizations with overdue reports.
Please complete this cover sheet, attach the narrative, an updated tracking matrix and final financial reports, and upload the PDF document to the grant portal “Reporting” section for this award. Direct questions to Jarissa Lum, Program Officer at 808-566-5522 or by email at jlum@hcf-hawaii.org.

 Financial report: ▪ Provide original project budget shown in your grant application ▪ Show all actual project income and expenditures ▪ Indicate expenses for which this Geist Foundation grant was used.
 Narrative report: ▪ Describe the youth outcome area(s) addressed (permanence, education, employment, housing, physical and mental health, personal and community engagement) and the outcomes you were trying to achieve. ▪ Provide the number of transitioning foster youth served by the project, in these age groups: 14-15, 1618, 19-21, 22-24 ▪ Describe the activities conducted and the services delivered, including numbers of youth participating. Explain any changes from the activities described in your grant application. (You must use the grant only for the purpose stated in the grant award letter.) ▪ Describe what happened as a result of the efforts (outcomes), including any differences between these results and the expected results described in your grant application. ▪ Describe challenges encountered, unexpected benefits, and lessons learned.
▪ Describe future plans for these efforts.
 Updated Tracking Matrix (PDF)

fields.reason: The records don't track how grant money was spent.

items.title: Youth outcome areas addressed
items.quote: Describe the youth outcome area(s) addressed (permanence, education, employment, housing, physical and mental health, personal and community engagement) and the outcomes you were trying to achieve.

fields.label: Youth outcome area(s) addressed
fields.quote: Describe the youth outcome area(s) addressed (permanence, education, employment, housing, physical and mental health, personal and community engagement)
fields.ask: Which youth outcome areas did this project address: permanence, education, employment, housing, health, or engagement?
fields.reason: Choosing the outcome areas the project targeted is a staff judgment that the records can't make.

fields.label: Outcomes you were trying to achieve
fields.quote: the outcomes you were trying to achieve
fields.ask: What outcomes did your grant application say this project aimed to achieve for transitioning foster youth?
fields.reason: The intended outcomes come from the grant application and staff judgment, and the records only show results, not what the program set out to achieve.

history.reason: The field asks which outcome areas the program targeted and what it intended to achieve, but the draft states as fact that the program aimed to build confidence (the records can't show intent, and the mapper itself says the intended outcomes come from the application), names none of the funder's outcome areas, reports results instead of goals, and treats {confidence_improved}, which is a percent, as a count in "{confidence_improved} of them."

items.title: Number of transitioning foster youth served
items.quote: Provide the number of transitioning foster youth served by the project, in these age groups: 14-15, 1618, 19-21, 22-24

fields.label: Youth served, ages 14-15
fields.quote: Provide the number of transitioning foster youth served by the project, in these age groups: 14-15
fields.missing: Foster care or transition status for each participant, and age bands that match 14-15 (the records use 13-15).
fields.reason: The records don't show who is a transitioning foster youth, and the 13-15 range doesn't line up with 14-15.

fields.label: Youth served, ages 16-18
fields.quote: Provide the number of transitioning foster youth served by the project, in these age groups: 14-15, 1618
fields.missing: Foster care or transition status for each participant.
fields.reason: The records hold a 16-18 age range but no foster status, so participants served would count youth who may not be in foster care.

fields.label: Youth served, ages 19-21
fields.quote: Provide the number of transitioning foster youth served by the project, in these age groups: 14-15, 1618, 19-21
fields.missing: Foster care or transition status for each participant, and age bands that split 19-21 from 22-24.
fields.reason: The records don't show foster status, and they only hold a combined 19-24 range.

fields.label: Youth served, ages 22-24
fields.quote: Provide the number of transitioning foster youth served by the project, in these age groups: 14-15, 1618, 19-21, 22-24
fields.missing: Foster care or transition status for each participant, and age bands that split 22-24 from 19-21.
fields.reason: The records don't show foster status, and they only hold a combined 19-24 range.

items.title: Activities conducted and services delivered
items.quote: Describe the activities conducted and the services delivered, including numbers of youth participating. Explain any changes from the activities described in your grant application.

fields.label: Activities conducted and services delivered
fields.quote: Describe the activities conducted and the services delivered
fields.text: During {period}, the program ran {sessions_delivered} mentoring and skills sessions across its Coding Club, Mentor Circle and Weekend Leaders groups, for a total of {participant_hours} participant hours. Participants also handed in {assignment_submissions} assignments.
fields.ask: What other services, beyond these group sessions, did transitioning foster youth receive during the grant?
fields.reason: Session, hours and assignment records can describe the activities delivered, with the group names taken from the Groups table.

history.reason: The draft describes the activities and services delivered using only supported slots (sessions delivered, participant hours, assignment submissions), and the three group names come from the Groups table.

fields.label: Numbers of youth participating
fields.reason: Participants served counts each youth who attended at least one session, which is the number of youth taking part in the activities.

history.reason: Participants served counts each youth once if they attended at least one session in the period, which matches the number of youth taking part in the activities.

fields.label: Changes from activities in grant application
fields.quote: Explain any changes from the activities described in your grant application.
fields.ask: How did the activities you delivered differ from those described in your grant application, and why?
fields.reason: The records do not include the grant application, so only staff can make this comparison.

items.title: Outcomes resulting from the efforts
items.quote: Describe what happened as a result of the efforts (outcomes), including any differences between these results and the expected results described in your grant application.

fields.label: Outcomes
fields.quote: Describe what happened as a result of the efforts (outcomes)
fields.text: Of the {participants_checked_in} participants who rated their confidence at intake and at a check-in during {period}, {confidence_improved} reported greater confidence at their latest check-in. The program kept {retention_rate} of the youth enrolled during the period through its last day.
fields.ask: What other outcomes did youth reach, such as housing, school or employment milestones?
fields.reason: Confidence check-ins and enrollment dates support outcome statements; staff can add outcomes the records don't track.

history.reason: The draft matches the metric definitions: confidence_improved (shown as a percent, 73% for Q3) is a share of the participants who have both an intake score and a check-in in the period, and retention_rate is the share of youth enrolled during the period who were still enrolled on its last day.

fields.label: Differences from expected results
fields.quote: including any differences between these results and the expected results described in your grant application.
fields.ask: How do these results differ from the expected results in your grant application, and why?
fields.reason: The expected results from the grant application are not in the records.

items.title: Challenges, unexpected benefits, lessons learned
items.quote: Describe challenges encountered, unexpected benefits, and lessons learned.

fields.label: Challenges encountered
fields.ask: What challenges did the program encounter in delivering these efforts?
fields.reason: Challenges are a staff judgment the records cannot supply.

fields.label: Unexpected benefits
fields.ask: What unexpected benefits came out of this work?
fields.reason: Unexpected benefits are a staff account the records do not hold.

fields.label: Lessons learned
fields.ask: What lessons did the program learn from this work?
fields.reason: Lessons learned are a staff reflection the records cannot provide.

items.title: Future plans for these efforts
items.quote: Describe future plans for these efforts.

fields.label: Future plans
fields.quote: Describe future plans for these efforts.
fields.ask: What are your future plans for continuing or changing these efforts?
fields.reason: Future plans need staff input and are not in the records.
